svg.text: In The Year 2000! cryptex: assembly and lock
Part outlines match the cut sheets. Build each sub-assembly apart, then put them together. Rings, washers and core stay loose. Not cutting templates.
Part IDs (the letter is the sub-assembly, the number, R (ring) or C (collar) is the layer from the bottom)
A1 x1: center of the floor, under the core
A2R x1: upper glued face, covered by the next base layer
A2C x1: upper glued face, covered by the next base layer
A3R x1: upper glued face, covered by the next base layer
A3C x1: upper glued face, covered by the next base layer
A4R x1: upper glued face, covered by the next base layer
A4C x1: upper glued face, covered by the next base layer
A5R x1: top of the rim, under the loose ring
A5C x1: top of the collar, under the loose washers
E1 x1: underside of the rim; blank reverse takes glue
(E2) x1: ring 1: the only digit slice left after B2, C2 and D2 are placed
D1 x1: underside of the rim; blank reverse takes glue
D2 x1: under the next ring up
C1 x1: underside of the rim; blank reverse takes glue
C2 x1: under the next ring up
B1 x1: underside of the rim; blank reverse takes glue
B2 x1: under the next ring up
G1B x1: upper glued face, covered by the upper washer
G1 x1: top of the upper washer; blank reverse takes glue
G2B x1: upper glued face, covered by the upper washer
G2 x1: top of the upper washer; blank reverse takes glue
G3B x1: upper glued face, covered by the upper washer
G3 x1: top of the upper washer; blank reverse takes glue
G4B x1: upper glued face, covered by the upper washer
G4 x1: top of the upper washer; blank reverse takes glue
(CORE0) x1: down face: hidden artwork, no ID
(CORER) x4: unmarked: glue face or no hidden space for an ID
(COREC) x8: unmarked: glue face or no hidden space for an ID
(HEAD) x1: down face: hidden artwork, no ID
(LID) x1: down face: hidden artwork, no ID
(LIDP) x2: unmarked: glue face or no hidden space for an ID
IDs use covered faces, including small marks on glue faces. Hidden pictures use unglued faces. Cut and engrave face up in one pass. During assembly
orient ring bottoms, CORE0 ceiling, head and bridge artwork down; other art faces up. Unmarked parts are in (brackets). Spread glue across the small
ID marks too.

g.text: Stack A: the base
A1
A2R
A2C
Glue the base stack from the bottom: A1, then A2R and A2C, up
to A5R and A5C. Keep the ridge slots of A2C to A5C lined up,
on the marker side (right).
It is the slowest to cure and carries the rest, so it goes
first, under a weight. Stand the dry core F in the slots as a
pin to line the collars up.
Sub-assembly A is one solid: a floor, a hollow ring and a
collar round the ridge slot.
Stacks B, C, D, E: the four rings
B1
B2
E1
E2
Glue ring 4 (stack B): B2 digits up over B1 artwork down,
outer edges flush. Glue only blank mating faces; keep glue off
the socket. Sub-assembly B is one solid: ring 4, a rim under
the digit slice.
Glue ring 3 (stack C): C2 digits up over C1 artwork down,
outer edges flush. Glue only blank mating faces; keep glue off
the socket. Sub-assembly C is one solid: ring 3, a rim under
the digit slice.
Glue ring 2 (stack D): D2 digits up over D1 artwork down,
outer edges flush. Glue only blank mating faces; keep glue off
the socket. Sub-assembly D is one solid: ring 2, a rim under
the digit slice.
Glue ring 1 (stack E): E2 digits up over E1 artwork down,
outer edges flush. Glue only blank mating faces; keep glue off
the socket. Sub-assembly E is one solid: ring 1, a rim under
the digit slice.
A ring must turn freely on the core, so it is glued to nothing
else. Rings are made apart and cure at the same time.
Stack F: the core
CORE0
CORER
COREC
Glue the 13 core slices from the bottom: four COREC, then
alternating CORER and COREC (four CORER, three COREC), one
more COREC, then solid CORE0 artwork down as the ceiling. Glue
only the blank wall annuli. Alternate plywood grain; no glue
in the bore or over the ceiling picture.
It is the one part that must stay straight and slide out of
the rings, so it is glued as a stack on a rolled tube that
lines up the holes.
Sub-assembly F is one solid: a tube open at the bottom, closed
at the top, with four aligned ridge tabs beneath the locking
faces.
G1 to G4: the washer pairs
G1
G2
Glue ID-marked G1B below artwork G1, artwork up and outer
decagon flats aligned (6.36 mm). Glue the mating faces,
including the small lower ID; keep the lower circular relief
and upper notch clean. Sub-assembly G1 is one solid washer for
ring 1.
Glue ID-marked G2B below artwork G2, artwork up and outer
decagon flats aligned (6.36 mm). Glue the mating faces,
including the small lower ID; keep the lower circular relief
and upper notch clean. Sub-assembly G2 is one solid washer for
ring 2.
Glue ID-marked G3B below artwork G3, artwork up and outer
decagon flats aligned (6.36 mm). Glue the mating faces,
including the small lower ID; keep the lower circular relief
and upper notch clean. Sub-assembly G3 is one solid washer for
ring 3.
Glue ID-marked G4B below artwork G4, artwork up and outer
decagon flats aligned (6.36 mm). Glue the mating faces,
including the small lower ID; keep the lower circular relief
and upper notch clean. Sub-assembly G4 is one solid washer for
ring 4.
Two washers make a part as thick as its ring, and the pair
stays loose so it can be lifted out and turned.
H head, I posts and J retaining bridge
HEAD
LID
LIDP
The head H is one slice. It has no sub-assembly.
The head H is ready.
Only the head is glued on the core, and it goes on last, above
the retaining bridge. The bridge captures the rings and
washers.
LIDP are two upright side posts. Dry-fit their feet in A1. The
mushroom heads point up, outside ring 4.
Posts I are ready to glue into A1 during final assembly.
The posts anchor the retaining bridge to the base, so the ring
stack cannot lift off A1.
LID is the retaining bridge, artwork down. It is one piece,
with a notched core passage and two post keyholes.
Bridge J stays unglued; it can be released only after the core
is unlocked and withdrawn.
The post heads trap the bridge vertically. The inserted core
blocks the sideways slide needed to release it.

svg.text: Final assembly: put the finished sub-assemblies together
1. Stack ring 4 (stack B) digits up, on base A. It must turn
freely; core F goes in after the bridge.
2. Drop washer pair G4 into the socket of ring 4, notch to the
marker. Do not glue it.
3. Stack ring 3 (stack C) digits up, on the previous ring. It
must turn freely; core F goes in after the bridge.
4. Drop washer pair G3 into the socket of ring 3, notch to the
marker. Do not glue it.
5. Stack ring 2 (stack D) digits up, on the previous ring. It
must turn freely; core F goes in after the bridge.
6. Drop washer pair G2 into the socket of ring 2, notch to the
marker. Do not glue it.
7. Stack ring 1 (stack E) digits up, on the previous ring. It
must turn freely; core F goes in after the bridge.
8. Drop washer pair G1 into the socket of ring 1, notch to the
marker. Do not glue it.
9. Glue the feet of both LIDP posts into A1. Let cure. Keep
the mushroom tops clean; no glue on the bridge.
10. With core F still out, shift bridge J 6 mm toward the
title edge, lower its wide keyholes over the post heads, then
slide it 6 mm back to center. Do not glue J. The core goes
through its passage next and blocks the release slide.
11. Dial 2000, then lower core F through the bridge, open end
down onto A1, its ridge tabs to the marker. The glued A1 floor
closes the bore. Do not glue the core.
12. Glue head H artwork down on the core, above the retaining
bridge. Glue only the blank core wall annulus; keep glue off
the bridge, rings and artwork. Let cure. To load a note, dial
2000 and pull only F with H. Load through the open bottom,
lower F over the note onto A1 and scramble the rings.
Set your own code
1. To set your own code, dial 2 0 0 0 and pull core F with
head H straight up and out. The bridge and posts stay on the
base.
2. Slide bridge J 6 mm toward the title edge. The core must be
out first.
3. Lift bridge J off the post heads and set it aside.
4. Lift ring 1 (stack E) off and set it aside. The washer pair
G1 stays loose.
5. Lift the washer pair G1 out of its socket.
6. Turn G1 so its notch lies under the digit you want. One
digit is 36 degrees: three digits moves the first digit from 2
to 5.
7. Drop G1 back in its socket.
8. Put ring 1 (stack E) back on, then dial it to the new
digit. Do the same for D and G2, C and G3, B and G4.
9. Lower bridge J through its wide keyholes over the post
heads, 6 mm toward the title edge.
10. Slide bridge J 6 mm back to center, with the post necks in
the narrow keyholes.
11. Push core F back through J. Read the code from ring 1 out
along the marker.

g.text: The lock: the ridge and a washer's notch (to scale)
Red: the core's ridge, at the marker. The washer is a ring's inner part.
Notch at the marker: the ridge passes
One digit off: the washer stops it
Setting and changing the combination
Seat each washer so its notch lies under the ring's digit you want.
Ring 1 (the smallest, on top) is the first digit and ring 4 the last,
read outward along the marker. It is set to 2000: ring 1 at 2, the rest at 0.
Each washer can sit ten ways, one per digit: 10,000 combinations.
The ridge is 4 mm wide, the notch 7 mm: a ring only has to be near its digit
(about 5 degrees), not exact. There are no detents, so look at the marker.

svg.text: Core height 41.34 mm: four pocket layers (12.72), eight ring slices (25.44), one ceiling (3.18). Stock 3.18 mm; fixed bridge above the rings, head above the bridge.
